x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Parliament can override a judgment only by changing the law or the constitutional basis of the ruling, and every such override is tested against the basic structure. Statement 1 is false: a simple resolution cannot overrule a judgment.

Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: nominated MPs and all Legislative Council members do not vote, while elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry do (70th Amendment, 1992). Statement 4 is false: only Delhi and Puducherry are named in the Explanation to Article 54, not every UT legislature.

Options A, B and C are duties of the Prime Minister under Article 78 (communicating Council decisions, furnishing information, and placing a minister's individual decision before the Council when the President requires). Administering the oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers is done by the President, not the PM.

The Constitution itself does not classify ministers into ranks; by convention the Council comprises Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State (Independent Charge), Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers. Deputy Prime Minister is not one of these ranks and is not mentioned in the Constitution; a Deputy PM takes oath as an ordinary minister.

The Prime Ministers from the Rajya Sabha were Indira Gandhi (the first, 1966), H.D. Deve Gowda, I.K. Gujral and Manmohan Singh. Charan Singh was a Lok Sabha member, not a Rajya Sabha PM (he is noted as the PM who never faced the Lok Sabha).

There are eight Cabinet Committees (Apr 2025): Appointments, Security, Political Affairs, Economic Affairs, Parliamentary Affairs, Accommodation, Investment and Growth, and Employment and Skill Development.
Goa, Mizoram and Sikkim have unicameral legislatures. Telangana, Karnataka and Maharashtra each have a Legislative Council, so options B, C and D each include a bicameral State.
